mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where real GDP growth declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production is associated with higher economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% in a month indicates a weakening demand for housing, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where housing starts decrease by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it indicates robust economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI increases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals a significant economic downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where real GDP growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3% in a month.
